npcs.name: Rook
npcs.title: a firebrand raging against the quiet dead's slow surrender
npcs.hail: *(A soul stands on the base of the milestone as on a barricade, and where every other soul in the grey is dimming, this one *burns* — not with Vesper's stolen warmth but with something hotter and its own: fury, banked and blazing, aimed at the whole grey machine. There is a scorched brazier beside them and a board nailed with the names of the faded, and they are, when your cold touches them, mid-sentence to an audience of the drifting dead who are mostly not listening.)* …*don't* you *DARE* *drift!* — *(they wheel on you, and the fury doesn't dim, it *focuses*)* …*YOU.* the *Returned.* the one who *crosses.* …*good*, *finally*, someone who's *SEEN* it from the *other* *side.* …*(they jab a finger at the drifting souls)* …*look* at them. *fading.* *quiet.* *peaceful.* …lining *up* to *dissolve* like it's *DIGNIFIED*, like *going* *gentle* into the *Wall* is some kind of — *(the fury cracks with something underneath)* …it's *SURRENDER*, cold one. every *soul* that *fades* *quiet* hands the *Wall* a *WIN.* …and i will *NOT.* …*i* *will* *not* *go* *quiet.* …and i'm *sick* to my *teeth* of *watching* *everyone* *else* *DO* it.

variants.text: *(They see something in your face — recognition — and their eyes narrow to blades.)* …you've *been* to the *bench.* …the *old* *woman.* *Oona.* …*(they say the name like a curse and a wound at once)* …*'finished.'* *'at* *peace.'* *'ready.'* …*(the fury spikes)* …she *SURRENDERED*, cold one. she looked at the *greatest* *injustice* in *creation* — a *Wall* that *EATS* the *unclaimed* for *NOTHING* — and she *tidied* her *accounts* and *sat* *DOWN* and *decided* to be *SERENE* about it. …*(shaking)* …and *everyone* *calls* it *wisdom.* they *garland* her. the *soul* who *made* *peace* with the *unforgivable.* …*(they round on you)* …*tell* me you *didn't* *catch* it. the *quiet.* the *giving*-*up* *dressed* as *grace.* …*tell* me you're not *going* *soft* on the *Wall* …because a *kind* *old* *woman* …*smiled* at you.

*(They look at you and something ignites — not sympathy, recognition, the recognition of one furnace for another.)* …*oh.* …*oh*, you *feel* it, don't you. the *cold.* …*(they step down off the milestone, toward you)* …*good.* *GOOD.* because here's what the *soft* ones won't *tell* you, cold one: the *cold* isn't *sadness.* it isn't *fading.* …the *cold* is *RAGE* with *nowhere* to *GO.* …*(fierce)* …you've been carrying *everyone's* *grief*, *swallowing* it, going *quiet* and *cold* — and the whole time there's been a *FIRE* in you and you've been *sitting* on it, *drowning* it, being *gentle* when you should be *BURNING.* …*(they grip your arm)* …*stop* *swallowing* it. …that *cold* you feel? …*give* it *AIR.* …*let* it *catch.* …you'll be *warmer* *furious* …than you *ever* were *kind.*

*(They size you up with the quick, hungry assessment of a recruiter who has learned to spot the ones who might carry the fire.)* …*(they don't soften, but they focus)* …you *cross*, they say. in and *out* of the *dark.* …then you *KNOW*, cold one — you *know* the *Wall* isn't *fate*, it isn't *justice*, it's a *CHOICE* some *dawn*-*age* *council* *made* and *everyone's* been *too* *TIRED* to *unmake.* …*(they gesture at the drifting dead)* …*they* don't *fight* it. they *drift.* they *fade* *polite.* …*i'm* *trying* to *WAKE* them, cold one. to *remind* them that a soul that *rages* *burns* *slower* than a soul that *sighs.* …*(fierce, pleading under the fury)* …*help* me. …or at the *very* *least* …*tell* me i'm *not* *mad* to *still* be *ANGRY* …when *everyone* *else* has *decided* to be *CALM* …about the *end* of *everything.*

nodes.speaker: Rook
nodes.text: *(They pace the milestone's base, all restless heat, and the argument pours out of them fully formed — you can tell they've made it a thousand times, to a thousand drifting souls who wouldn't listen.)* …*here's* the *arithmetic* the *calm* ones *ignore.* the *Wall* *runs* on *the* *forgotten.* on souls too *tired* to *hold* onto *themselves.* every one that *fades* *quiet* — *content*, *finished*, *at* *peace* — is *one* more *stone* in the *thing.* …*(they stab a finger at the board of names)* …so i *keep* them. i *write* the *faded* down. i *stand* here and i *SHOUT* and i make the *drifting* ones *ANGRY* enough to *stay* another *day*, and *another* — because *anger* is the *one* *fuel* the *Wall* can't *digest.* …*(their voice rises, cracks)* …they *call* me *mad.* they *call* me *unable* to *let* *go.* …but *SOMEONE* has to *refuse.* someone has to *stand* in the *middle* of the *quiet* *dying* and *SCREAM* that it's *WRONG.* …*(they round on you, blazing)* …*am* i *wrong* to? …*is* the *rage* the *madness* …*or* is the *CALM?*

choices.text: *(read the firebrand — past the fury, to what it's built on and what it's for)* "Hold still one second, Rook. Let me look at you — past the fire. At what you're actually burning."

*(the one who crosses, who has stood where the fire is going)* "I'll tell you what I've seen, Rook, since I cross both ways: I've met the soul you'll become if the rage is all you've got. There's a grey woman down the road who burned exactly like you, for a century, and there's nothing left of her but the ash. Before you recruit me, come meet your own future. Then tell me it's the fuel you think it is."

*(fan the flames — they're right, and the calm IS complicity)* "You're not mad, Rook. You're the only sane soul in a field of the anesthetized. A Wall that eats the innocent doesn't deserve your peace — it deserves your fury, and everyone else's. Show me the board. Let's make more of the drifting ones angry."

"Some of them have earned their rest, Rook. Oona finished — closed her accounts, said her sorrys. That's not surrender to the Wall. That's a soul the Wall couldn't catch because there was nothing left unfinished for it to grab. Peace isn't always giving up. Sometimes it's the only real win there is."

*(the thing under the fire — that rage is grief he can't afford to feel, and the real fight is to grieve the thing, and let the grief aim the fire instead of the denial)* "Here's what I think you already know, Rook, and can't stand still long enough to feel. You're not raging at the Wall. You're raging so you never have to stop and grieve whatever it took from you — because grief means being still, and being still means feeling it, and the fury is the one thing loud enough to drown that out. Your rage isn't wrong. But it's aimed at the wrong thing. Grieve what you lost. Actually grieve it. And then — I promise you — the fire won't go out. It'll finally have somewhere true to point."
"Let me walk a moment, Rook. There's someone down the road I want to see first."

nodes.speaker: Rook
nodes.text: *(They hold still — it costs them visibly, stillness being the one thing the fire cannot abide — and your sense goes into the blaze and finds the fuel at the bottom of it.)* *(And you find, first, that the cause is real. The rage is not a lie or a pose; the Wall *is* an atrocity, and Rook sees it clearly, and the fury at it is the most honest response in the grey — you cannot fault the target. But your sense reads what the fire is built on, the log at the very bottom that everything else is stacked to keep burning, and it is not the Wall at all. It is a single grief. Someone Rook loved — your sense reads the shape of it, a person, close, beloved — faded. Went quiet. Drifted into the Wall gentle and content and *at peace*, exactly the way Rook now cannot forgive the drifting dead for doing — and Rook stood there and watched the person they loved most choose serenity over staying, choose to let go, and could not stop it, and has never, for one single instant since, stopped moving long enough to feel it. And your sense reads the terrible engine of it: that the rage is not despite the grief but *because* of it — that Rook discovered, in the hour of that loss, that fury is loud enough to drown grief out, that a soul screaming at a Wall cannot simultaneously feel the specific unbearable ache of one beloved face going gentle into it, and so Rook has kept screaming, for however long it has been, running the fire at full roar precisely so that the stillness — in which the grief lives — can never once fall. And your sense reads the thing that would free them and that they are most terrified of: that if they stopped, just once, and let themselves grieve the actual person instead of raging at the abstract Wall, the fire would not go out. It would clarify. It would stop being a wall of noise against feeling and become a clean, aimed, grief-fed flame — the difference between a soul burning to avoid its pain and a soul burning *for* something. But to get there they would have to hold still, and feel the one thing the whole inferno was built to outrun.)*

nodes.speaker: Rook
nodes.text: *(The mention of the grey woman lands like cold water, and for a moment the fire gutters — not out, but low, exposing something wary underneath.)* …a soul who *burned* like me. …*(they don't want to ask, and ask anyway)* …*'nothing* *left* but *ash.'* …*(the fury flickers back up, defensive)* …*good.* *let* her be *ash.* better *ash* than *SURRENDER*, better *burned*-*out* than *bowed*-*DOWN* — …*(but the wariness stays, under it)* …*(quieter)* …i've — i've *seen* her, i think. down the *road.* the *grey* one. the one who *doesn't* *shout* anymore, just …*sits*, all *hollow.* …i've been *not*-*looking* at her for a *long* *while.* …*(they meet your eyes, and the fear shows)* …you think that's — you think that's where the *fire* *goes.* …*(a beat)* …*go* on, then, cold one. *see* her. and *come* *back* and *tell* me — *honestly* — …*is* she *ash* because she *burned?* …*or* because she *burned* the *WRONG* *thing?*

nodes.speaker: Rook
nodes.text: *(You tell them they're right, and the effect is enormous — a firebrand who has shouted into a thousand deaf drifts, suddenly, unbearably, *heard.*)* …*(they seize your hand, blazing)* …*YES.* …*yes*, cold one, *finally* — a *Returned*, one who's *SEEN* it, standing with the *fire* instead of *telling* me to *put* it *out.* …*(they pull you toward the board of names)* …*look.* every one of these was a soul who was *drifting* *quiet* and i made them *ANGRY* enough to *stay* *another* *day.* …*(fierce, alight)* …it *WORKS*, cold one. a *roused* soul *burns* *slower.* *rage* is the *one* *rebellion* the *Wall* can't *eat.* …*(they hand you a nail and a name)* …*help* me *wake* them. *stand* on the *stone* and *SHOUT* with me. …*(and you do, for a while, and it feels like the truest thing you've done — souls lifting their heads, catching the fire, refusing to fade)* …*(and it works, and it is real, and only much later, on the road, will you wonder what happens to a field of the furious when the one who lit them finally burns out — and whether you fanned a rebellion, or just taught a hundred grieving souls a louder way to never heal.)*

nodes.speaker: Rook
nodes.text: *(The defense of Oona hits them hard, and the fury flares to cover something rawer.)* …*'nothing* *left* *unfinished* for it to *GRAB.'* …*(they laugh, and it is a terrible sound)* …*oh*, that's — that's the *cleverest* *surrender* i ever *heard.* *'close* your *accounts* and the *Wall* can't *catch* you.' …*(shaking)* …you know what that *IS*, cold one? that's the *Wall* *teaching* the *dead* to *pre*-*digest* *themselves.* to *tidy* up so *nicely* they *fall* into the *machine* without a *fight.* …*(and then, under the fury, the wound flexes)* …*(quieter, cracking)* …*she* *finished.* the *person* — …*(they stop, hard)* …*someone* i — *someone* *finished* like *that.* *serene.* *ready.* *let* *go* while i *SCREAMED* at them to *STAY.* …and everyone said *'let* them *have* their *peace'* — …*(the rage is trembling now, thin over something enormous)* …*don't* *tell* me *peace* is a *win*, cold one. …*peace* is what they *called* it …when the *person* i *loved* …*chose* the *Wall* …over *staying* …with *me.*

nodes.speaker: Rook
nodes.text: *(You don't tell them to calm down — you tell them to grieve, and to keep the fire — and a firebrand braced for a thousandth argument about letting go hears, instead, permission to burn *and* to hurt, and it stops them cold.)* …*(the fury falters, and for the first time since you met them, Rook goes still)* …*grieve* *it.* …*(barely)* …*i* — i *can't.* if i *stop* *moving* i'll — …*(and then, because you're still there, because you said the fire could stay, they stop moving)* …*(and it hits them, all of it, the thing the inferno was built to outrun — one beloved face going gentle into the Wall while they screamed — and they double over with it, and it is not rage now, it is grief, huge and specific and years overdue)* …*(they weep, and the fire does not go out; it *changes*, the wild roar of it settling into something with a center)* …*(a long time later, they straighten, and the eyes are wet and clear and still burning, but *aimed* now)* …*you're* *right.* …i've been *screaming* at a *Wall* …so i'd never have to *feel* *one* *face.* …*(a shaking breath)* …and the *screaming* *never* — it never *touched* the *Wall*, did it. it just kept *me* from — …*(they look at the board of names, and then at you, transformed)* …*the* *fire* *stays.* …but it's not *noise* anymore. …i *lost* someone to that *thing*, cold one. *specifically.* by *name.* and i'm going to spend what's *left* of me *fighting* it *for* *them* …instead of *screaming* to *forget* them. …*(fierce, and grieving, and finally whole)* …*that's* a *fire* that *warms* instead of just *burns.* …*thank* you …for *letting* me *keep* it …*and* *mourn.*

nodes.speaker: Rook
nodes.text: *(You find the exact seam — not calm the fire, aim it; not stop grieving, start — and a soul who has run at full roar for years to outrun one unbearable stillness finally, in front of you, stops running, and the collapse and the clarity arrive in the same breath.)* …*(they go down onto the milestone's step, the fury draining and the grief flooding the space it leaves, and they say a name — one name, a person's name, the log at the bottom of the whole fire — and then they simply, at last, mourn)* …*(and you sit with them while they do, and it takes a long time, and the drifting dead drift on, and for once Rook does not shout at them, because Rook is doing the one thing louder than shouting: feeling)* …*(and when it is done, they are not extinguished — they are *forged*, the wild scattered heat of them hammered into a single edge)* …*(they stand, and look at the board of the faded, and at the Wall on the horizon, and their voice when it comes is quiet, and it is the most dangerous thing you have heard in the grey)* …*i don't need to *SHOUT* anymore. …*(a grief-clear certainty)* …*shouting* was for *drowning* it *out.* now that i've *felt* it …i can *hear* myself *think.* …and *thinking*, cold one — *(a small, terrible, purposeful smile)* …*thinking* is what the *Wall* should have been *afraid* of *all* *along.* i know its *shape* now. i know *who* it *took* from me and *how* and *why* the *dawn*-*age* *cowards* *built* it. …i'm going to *stop* *rousing* the *drifting* to *rage* …and start *teaching* them to *REMEMBER.* …because a soul that's *held* in *memory* *doesn't* *fade* …and *that*, not *anger*, is the *fire* the *Wall* can't *eat.* …*(they offer you their hand, grieving and blazing and clear)* …you didn't put my *fire* *out*, cold one. …you gave it *EYES.*

nodes.speaker: Rook
nodes.text: *(The insight is true but you deliver it like a diagnosis — *your rage is really grief* — and a soul who has weaponized fury for years turns that very weapon on the messenger.)* …*(the fire flares, defensive)* …*oh*, that's *convenient.* *'you're* not *really* *angry*, you're just *sad*, there there, have a *cry* and *stop* *making* a *scene.'* …*(scornful, wounded)* …that's what they *ALL* say, cold one. it's how they've *always* *shut* me *up* — call the *rage* a *symptom*, call the *grief* the *real* thing, and *poof*, the *inconvenient* *fury* becomes a *feeling* to be *managed* instead of a *TRUTH* to be *reckoned* with. …*(but the flare is a beat too fast, a shade too defensive, and you both feel it)* …*(quieter, grudging)* …*come* *back*, cold one. …and next time don't tell me my *rage* is *hiding* something. …tell me — *(they struggle)* …tell me i'm *allowed* to *have* *both.* the *fire* *and* the — …*(they can't say it)* …*(the) other thing. maybe then i'd — no. go. i need to not have heard that for a while.)*

nodes.speaker: Rook
nodes.text: *(The fire is still up, but it's guttering at the edges now, and they keep glancing down the road toward the grey woman they've been not-looking at.)* …*(gruffly)* …you *rattled* something. i'll not *pretend* you *didn't.* …*(they poke at the scorched brazier)* …i've been *running* this *fire* *so* *long* i *forgot* it was ever *lit* *FROM* *something.* …*(a hard breath)* …*go* see the *grey* one. *Cinder.* down the *road.* …*(quieter)* …and *come* *back*, cold one. …because if you're *right* — if there's a way to *keep* the *fire* *and* *feel* the — the *thing* under it — …*(they can't quite hope out loud)* …then i've been *doing* this *wrong* …for a *very* …*long* …*time.* …and i'd *rather* *know* …than *burn* *out* *not*-*knowing* …like *her.*

nodes.speaker: Rook
nodes.text: *(You overplay it — go soft and knowing, *let it out, you'll feel so much better* — and a firebrand hears condescension and slams the furnace door.)* …*don't.* …*(cold now, which is worse than the heat)* …don't you *therapize* me, cold one. don't you stand in a *field* of the *quietly* *dying* and tell the *one* soul still *FIGHTING* that they'd feel *ever* so much *better* if they'd just *have* a *little* *cry* and *calm* *DOWN.* …*(furious, closed)* …that's the *Wall's* *own* *voice*, that is. *'calm* *down.* *let* *go.* *make* your *peace.'* …it's what it *WHISPERS* to *every* soul it *EATS.* …*(they turn back to their audience of the drifting)* …*go* *drift* with the *rest* of them if you *want* *peace* so *badly.* …*(and then, so low you barely catch it, the wound showing through the armor one last time)* …*(…i know it's under there. the grief. i KNOW. i'm not a fool. but you came at it like it was a WEAKNESS to be fixed, and it's not, it's the most PRECIOUS thing i have and you reached for it like a NURSE. come back when you understand it's not a wound to be lanced. it's a person. go.)*

nodes.speaker: Rook
nodes.text: *(They wave you off, already turning back to the drifting dead, the fire roaring back up to fill the space where you stood.)* …*go*, then. …*everyone* *goes.* …*(and then, over their shoulder, fierce and alone)* …but *hear* me, cold one — *whatever* you *decide* about me — *don't* you *drift.* …*(and they mean it as a battle-cry, and it comes out, underneath, as a plea)* …*whatever* *else* …*don't* you *fade* *quiet* *too.* …i can't — *(they catch it)* …i'm *tired* of *watching* *everyone* i *talk* to …*go* *soft* …and *drift* …*away.*

nodes.speaker: Cinder
nodes.text: *(A soul sits in the grey a little way down from the firebrand's noise — and where Rook blazes, this one is the after: grey to the bone, hollow, a face like a hearth the morning after, all cold ash and the ghost of heat. She looks up at you with eyes that have done all their burning.)* …*(her voice is quiet, worn smooth)* …you've been *up* the *road.* with the *shouting* one. *Rook.* …*(the faintest, tiredest smile)* …i can *always* *tell.* the *ones* who've *heard* *Rook* come *down* here *lit*, all *fired* *up*, wanting me to *agree* the *rage* is *righteous.* …*(she shakes her head, slow)* …i was *Rook*, cold one. …*(simply)* …a *hundred* *years* ago, or *more*, i *stood* on that *same* *stone* and *SHOUTED* at the *same* *Wall* and *made* the *same* *drifting* *souls* *ANGRY* and *called* it a *rebellion.* …*(she spreads her grey hands)* …*this* is *how* it *ends.* …*ask*, if you *want.* …i've *nothing* *left* to *burn*, so i've *nothing* *left* to *lie* *for.*

choices.text: *(read the burned-out fire — what a century of rage actually costs)* "Let me look at you, Cinder. At what the fire left. I need to understand where that road ends — I've got someone up it."

*(the one who crosses)* "I'm the soul the Wall gave back, Cinder. I can carry things between souls who can't reach each other. Rook won't come down here — won't look at you, calls you their future and can't stand to see it. Is there something you'd have me carry up the road? Some word the firebrand needs before they burn to what you are?"
"Do you regret it, Cinder? The century of rage. Would you take it back?"
"What went wrong, Cinder? The fire — you're saying it wasn't worth it. Why not?"
"Rest, Cinder. I'll leave you to your quiet."

nodes.speaker: Cinder
nodes.text: *(She lets you look, indifferent, having nothing left to guard, and your sense moves into the cold hearth of her and reads the whole arc of a fire that burned to nothing.)* *(And you find that the rage was real, and the cause was just, and none of that saved her. Your sense reads a soul who lost someone — the same shape as Rook's wound, a beloved who faded gentle into the Wall — and who discovered that fury could drown the grief, and chose the fury, for a year, and then a decade, and then a century, screaming at the Wall so she would never have to feel the one face going quiet. And your sense reads what that century did: that rage, run long enough with nothing under it but the refusal to grieve, does not stay hot. It consumes its own fuel. It burns through the anger, and then through the memory of what the anger was for, and then through the beloved face itself — because she had used that face as kindling, screaming at its going instead of holding its having-been, and a memory used as fuel is a memory *spent* — until at last she cannot even remember, clearly, the name of the person she spent a hundred years being furious about. The grief she refused to feel did not go away; it went *cold*, and took the love with it, and left her this: a grey hollow that raged so hard and so long at a Wall that it forgot the one warm thing the rage was ever *for.* And your sense reads the one mercy still in her, the reason she sits here warning the newly-lit: that she knows, now, at the ash-end of it, exactly what she did wrong. Not that she was angry. That she was *only* angry. That she let the fire become a way to not-feel instead of a way to fight, and that if she could do it again she would let herself grieve the face first — grieve it whole, and keep it — and burn *for* it, not *through* it.)*

nodes.speaker: Cinder
nodes.text: *(Something stirs in the cold ash of her — not heat, but the memory of its shape.)* …a *word* for *Rook.* …*(she is quiet a long moment, gathering what's left)* …*yes.* …*carry* them *this*, cold one, from the *soul* they're *terrified* to *become:* …*(her worn voice finds an edge, the last ember)* …tell *Rook* i *don't* *regret* the *fighting.* the *Wall* *deserved* every *year* of it. …tell them the *fighting* was *right.* …but tell them i made *one* *mistake*, and it *cost* me *everything* the *fighting* was *for.* …*(barely)* …i used the *face* of the *one* i *lost* …as *firewood.* i *screamed* at their *fading* instead of *holding* their *having*-*lived* …and i *burned* the *memory* *up* to *keep* the *rage* *hot* …until i couldn't *remember* …*who* i was *angry* *for.* …*(she looks at you, hollow and urgent at once)* …*tell* Rook: *grieve* them *first.* *keep* the *face.* *then* *burn.* …a fire *fed* on *grief* *you've* *let* *yourself* *feel* …lasts *forever* and *warms* you. …a fire fed on grief *refused* …*eats* the *very* *thing* …you *lit* it *for.* …*go.* …*tell* them …*before* they *forget* …the *name* they're *fighting* for. …the way *i* …*(she stops, and cannot finish, because she has)*

nodes.speaker: Cinder
nodes.text: *(She considers it with the flat honesty of someone with nothing left to protect.)* …*regret* it. …*(slowly)* …*no.* and *yes.* …*(she folds her grey hands)* …i don't *regret* the *anger.* the *Wall* is an *obscenity* and being *furious* at it was the *truest* thing i ever *felt.* a soul that *doesn't* *rage* at *that* isn't *calm*, it's *asleep.* …*(then the ash-cold sets in)* …but i *regret* what i *let* the *anger* *do* to me. …i made it my *whole* *self.* i let it *burn* through everything *else* — the *grief*, the *love*, the *face* — until there was *nothing* left but the *burning*, and then the *burning* ran out of *fuel*, and *this* is what's *under* it. …*(she gestures at her own grey hollowness)* …*ash.* …*(she meets your eyes)* …*that's* the *regret*, cold one. not that i *fought.* that i *fought* *so* *hard* i *forgot* to *keep* the *thing* i was *fighting* *for.* …*don't* let the *shouting* one …make the *same* …*trade.*

nodes.speaker: Cinder
nodes.text: *(She tells it plainly, a warning worn smooth by repetition to souls who mostly don't heed it.)* …what went *wrong.* …*(she nods)* …the *fire* itself was never *wrong*, cold one. that's the *trap* of it — everyone who tries to *cool* me down is *wrong*, the *rage* is *justified*, so i *never* *listened.* …*(a grey breath)* …what went *wrong* is *what* the *fire* was *for.* …i lit it to *avoid* a *grief.* someone i *loved* *faded*, *gentle*, *chose* the *Wall*, and i couldn't *bear* to *feel* it — so i got *ANGRY* instead, because *anger* *stands* *UP* and *grief* just *lies* you *DOWN.* …*(the ember gutters)* …and a fire lit to *avoid* a feeling has to *keep* *burning* *forever*, because the *second* it *stops*, the *feeling's* *still* *there*, *waiting.* …so it *never* *stops.* …and it *eats* *everything.* …*(she looks up the road, toward Rook's distant blaze)* …*that* one's doing it *now.* burning so they never have to *feel* the *one* they *lost.* …and it'll *work* …*right* up until there's *nothing* *left* to *burn* …*but* the *one* they *lost.*

nodes.speaker: Cinder
nodes.text: *(She nods, and settles back into her grey quiet, the ash of a fire that warmed no one at the end, not even herself.)* …*go* on. …*(the tired ghost of a smile)* …*mind* the *shouting* one, cold one. …*(quietly)* …they *think* i'm their *enemy* — the *cautionary* *tale*, the *sell*-*out*, the *ash.* …*(she shakes her head)* …i'm *not.* i'm the *only* soul on this *road* …who *loves* them *enough* …to be *terrified* *for* them. …*(she looks up the road at the blaze)* …*tell* them, if you *can:* …the *ash* …*isn't* *angry* *at* them. …the *ash* …just *remembers* …*being* them. …and *wishes* …*someone* had *told* *it* …*how* to *grieve* …*before* it *forgot* *who* *for.*
